📘 traffic-ticket-contest Docs

A production-grade ERB platform (admin/state-machine/jurisdiction/routing/feature-catalog machinery, extracted from the industrial-ui-services portal) with traffic-ticket contest as the example domain. The platform tables carry the full production conventions; tickets are one domain riding on top.

Declarative business rules rendered from the rulebook — the single source of truth. Every statement below is the plain-language reading of a formula; nothing here is hand-authored prose.

Use the in the top-right corner to turn each part of the documentation on or off — Docs, the literal reading, the raw formula, the author's description, and the links to a rule's inputs and consumers. Your choices are remembered.

Business Rule

A business rule is identified by its name and is related to optionally a business rule category (its category).

ƒ Name Calculated 1 hop from ground truth string DR-1

Logical key — lowercased rule code.

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

A business rule's name is computed as the lower-cased rule code with every a space replaced by a hyphen.

In plain words

Rule code with “ ” replaced by “-” lowercased.

As a formula
= LOWER(SUBSTITUTE(Rule Code, " ", "-"))

Audit Log Entry

An audit log entry is identified by its name and is related to optionally a citation and optionally an app user (its actor).

ƒ Name Calculated 1 hop from ground truth string DR-9

Logical key.

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

An audit log entry's name is computed as the lower-cased “audit-”, followed by the citation, followed by a hyphen, followed by the timestamp formatted as “YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm-ss”, followed by a hyphen, followed by the action type with every a space replaced by a hyphen.

In plain words

((((("audit-" joined with citation) joined with "-") joined with datetime_format(timestamp, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm-ss")) joined with "-") joined with action type) with “ ” replaced by “-” lowercased.

As a formula
= LOWER(SUBSTITUTE("audit-" & Citation & "-" & DATETIME_FORMAT(Timestamp, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH-mm-ss") & "-" & Action Type, " ", "-"))
Inputs 3 fields this rule reads
⇢CitationAudit Log Entry FK to the Citation this audit entry concerns. ●TimestampAudit Log Entry When the action occurred. ●Action TypeAudit Log Entry STATUS_CHANGE | field-edit | OVERRIDE | review-decision | recommendation-change | SUBMISSION | hard-stop-block.
Ground truth at the leaves 3 the raw values this ultimately depends on
⇢ Citation Audit Log Entry ● Timestamp Audit Log Entry ● Action Type Audit Log Entry

FK to the Citation this audit entry concerns.

A pointer to Citation. It is not derived from anything else — it is the link the rest of the DAG hangs off.

Consumers 2 direct rules that read this one
ƒ Name Audit Log Entry ƒ Is Override Action Audit Log Entry
● From Value Ground truth string

Previous value (if applicable).

● To Value Ground truth string

New value (if applicable).

● Reason Ground truth string

Reason text — required for OVERRIDE.

ƒ Is Override Action Calculated 1 hop from ground truth boolean DR-10

Calculated flag — TRUE when this audit log entry represents a manager override action (vs a routine action).

In Docs

The audit log entry's is override action is determined by the following priority:

  1. true if the action type, followed by an empty string is “override”
  2. false in all other cases
In plain words

If (action type joined with "") lowercased is "override" then true(), otherwise false().

As a formula
= IF(LOWER(Action Type & "") = "override", TRUE(), FALSE())
Inputs 1 fields this rule reads
●Action TypeAudit Log Entry STATUS_CHANGE | field-edit | OVERRIDE | review-decision | recommendation-change | SUBMISSION | hard-stop-block.
Ground truth at the leaves 1 the raw values this ultimately depends on
● Action Type Audit Log Entry
ƒ Entry Age Hours Calculated 1 hop from ground truth integer DR-11

Calculated — hours elapsed since EntryTimestamp. Used to age audit log entries.

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

An audit log entry's entry age hours is computed as the number of hours from the timestamp to the current date and time.

In plain words

Datetime_diff(now, timestamp, "hours").

As a formula
= DATETIME_DIFF(NOW(), Timestamp, 'hours')

ƒ Depth Calculated 1 hop from ground truth integer DR-31

Calculated — nesting depth in the menu tree. 0 = top-level (no parent); otherwise the number of dot-segments in the dotted RouteKey above the root (e.g. 'library.rules.detail' = 2). Drives N-deep indentation.

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

The platform naviation's depth is determined by the following priority:

  1. 0 if the parent route key is blank
  2. the length of the route key minus the length of the route key with every a period replaced by an empty string in all other cases
In plain words

If parent route key equals blank() then 0, otherwise (the length of route key minus the length of route key with “.” replaced by “”).

As a formula
= IF(Parent Route Key=BLANK(), 0, LEN(Route Key) - LEN(SUBSTITUTE(Route Key, ".", "")))
Inputs 2 fields this rule reads
●Parent Route KeyPlatform Naviation Route key of parent nav node (empty for top-level) ●Route KeyPlatform Naviation Stable dot-delimited slug, e.g. checklists.score
Ground truth at the leaves 2 the raw values this ultimately depends on
● Parent Route Key Platform Naviation ● Route Key Platform Naviation
ƒ Full Path Calculated 1 hop from ground truth string DR-32

Calculated — canonical role-agnostic URL path (equals Route). The SPA renders this under each permitted role as /:role + FullPath and resolves it only when that role's *CanRead is true; the role is an implicit prefix, never stored on the row.

In Docs

A platform naviation's full path is the same as its route.

In plain words

Route.

As a formula
= Route

ƒ Handler Base Name Calculated 1 hop from ground truth string DR-33

Calculated — space-delimited form of the dotted RouteKey (dots and hyphens become spaces), e.g. 'library rules detail'. The client PascalCases this and prefixes the viewer role to derive the handler component deterministically: {Role} + PascalCase(HandlerBaseName) -> e.g. AdminLibraryRulesDetail, RepresentativeLibraryRulesDetail. No per-role handler is stored; edge cases get their own single-role route row instead.

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

A platform naviation's handler base name is computed as the route key with every a period replaced by a space with every a hyphen replaced by a space.

In plain words

Route key with “.” replaced by “ ” with “-” replaced by “ ”.

As a formula
= SUBSTITUTE(SUBSTITUTE(Route Key, ".", " "), "-", " ")

Generalizes the old =NOT(ToStage="DRAFT"): TRUE when ToStateKey is not the machine's initial state.

In Docs

A state transition is considered a forward if all of the following:

    • it is not the case that the to state key is “draft”
    • it is not the case that the to state key is “new”
    • it is not the case that the to state key is “pending”
    • it is not the case that the to state key is “open”
    • it is not the case that the to state key is “issued”
In plain words

Not to state key is "draft", not to state key is "new", not to state key is "pending", not to state key is "open", and not to state key is "issued".

As a formula

ƒ Due in Days Calculated 1 hop from ground truth integer DR-70

Calculated — days until DueDate (negative when overdue).

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

A work queue item's due in days is computed as the number of days from today's date to the due date.

In plain words

Datetime_diff(due date, today, "days").

As a formula
= DATETIME_DIFF(Due Date, TODAY(), 'days')
Inputs 1 fields this rule reads
●Due DateWork Queue Item Due date carried from the subject (e.g. Citations.PaymentDueDate, Citations.ResponseDueDate).
Consumers 2 direct +1 transitive rules that read this one
ƒ Is Overdue Work Queue Item ƒ Urgency Bucket Work Queue Item Is Urgent Work Queue Item

⇢ Assigned to Relationship string

FK -> AppUsers.AppUserId — the AppUser who owns this work item.

A pointer to App User. It is not derived from anything else — it is the link the rest of the DAG hangs off.

ƒ Is Overdue Calculated 2 hops from ground truth boolean DR-71

TRUE when DueInDays < 0.

In Docs

The work queue item's is overdue is determined by the following priority:

  1. false if the due in days is blank
  2. the due in days is less than 0 in all other cases
In plain words

If due in days equals blank() then false(), otherwise due in days is less than 0.

As a formula
= IF(Due in Days=BLANK(),FALSE(),Due in Days<0)
Inputs 1 fields this rule reads
ƒDue in DaysWork Queue Item Datetime_diff(due date, today, "days").
Ground truth at the leaves 1 the raw values this ultimately depends on
● Due Date Work Queue Item
ƒ Urgency Bucket Calculated 2 hops from ground truth string DR-72

URGENT (overdue or due today) / DUE_3_DAYS / UPCOMING / FOLLOW_UP (no due date).

In Docs

The work queue item's urgency bucket is determined by the following priority:

  1. “follow-up” if the due in days is blank
  2. “urgent” if the due in days is at most 0
  3. “due-3-days” if the due in days is at most 3
  4. “upcoming” in all other cases
In plain words

If due in days equals blank() then "follow-up", otherwise if due in days is at most 0 then "urgent", otherwise if due in days is at most 3 then "due-3-days", otherwise "upcoming".

As a formula
= IF(Due in Days=BLANK(),"follow-up",IF(Due in Days<=0,"urgent",IF(Due in Days<=3,"due-3-days","upcoming")))
Inputs 1 fields this rule reads
ƒDue in DaysWork Queue Item Datetime_diff(due date, today, "days").
Consumers 1 direct rules that read this one
ƒ Is Urgent Work Queue Item
Ground truth at the leaves 1 the raw values this ultimately depends on
● Due Date Work Queue Item
ƒ Is Urgent Calculated 3 hops from ground truth boolean DR-73

TRUE when UrgencyBucket = URGENT.

In Docs

A work queue item is considered urgent if the urgency bucket is “urgent”.

In plain words

Urgency bucket is "urgent".

As a formula

Intake & Response Shipped Delivered and live. true 1 false TT-INTAKE-01,TT-INTAKE-02,TT-DEADLINE-01 Records a new traffic citation as a row in the Citations table -- driver (FK to Drivers), violation type (FK to ViolationTypes), issuing jurisdiction (FK to Jurisdictions), and issue date -- and immediately derives the response deadline from the jurisdiction's DaysToRespond rule via vw_citations. An admin or representative captures the citation off a paper ticket and the computed ResponseDeadline column appears the moment the row is saved, with no manual date math. This is the front door of the whole citation-lifecycle state machine. README.md /assets/feature-images/citation-intake.png 2026-06-06T12:00:00Z admin-example 2026-06-06T12:00:00Z admin-example —
driver-response /citations/:citationId /citations/:citationId true true Driver Response Capture the driver's choice — pay now or request a hearing — and advance the citation from Issued to Responded before the response window closes. Intake & Response Shipped Delivered and live. true 2 false TT-INTAKE-03,TT-CONTEST-01 Captures the driver's choice -- pay now or request a hearing -- writing it onto the Citations row and advancing the citation from Issued to Responded in vw_citations before the response window closes. A representative records the decision on behalf of the cited driver, and the contest-track state machine branches on it. The response and its timestamp become CaseEvents rows so the audit trail explains every move. README.md /assets/feature-images/driver-response.png 2026-06-06T12:00:00Z admin-example 2026-06-06T12:00:00Z admin-example —
citation-statemachine /citations/:citationId /citations/:citationId true true Citation Lifecycle Tracker Show the live Citation status (Issued → Responded → InContest → Adjudicated → Closed) re-derived from facts and child events — never a stored, drifting column. State Machines Shipped Delivered and live. true 3 false TT-CITATION-01,TT-CITATION-02 Shows the live Citation status (Issued -> Responded -> InContest -> Adjudicated -> Closed) re-derived on every read from facts and child CaseEvents rows in vw_citations -- never a stored, drifting column. A user opens a citation and sees a glowing status path that always reflects current reality. The same computed CitationStatus column drives the work queue and the dashboards. ⇢ ERB Fields Relationship string

● Created At Ground truth datetime

Audit: when this row was first inserted. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on INSERT); immutable thereafter.

● Created by Ground truth string

Audit: the OWNER — the JWT user (auth.email()) who created this row. Auto-stamped on INSERT; immutable thereafter. NULL for build-time seed rows (no signed-in user).

● Modified At Ground truth datetime

Audit: when this row was last written. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on every INSERT/UPDATE).

● Modified by Ground truth string

Audit: the JWT user (auth.email()) who last wrote this row. Auto-stamped on every INSERT/UPDATE.

● Modified by Model Ground truth string

Audit: the AI model credited on the last save when an LLM made/assisted the change (e.g. "gpt-4o"). NULL for plain human writes. Read from the app.modified_by_model session GUC by the audit trigger. The owner (CreatedBy/ModifiedBy) is always the human JWT user, never a model.

Audit: when this row was first inserted. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on INSERT); immutable thereafter.

● Modified by Ground truth string

Audit: the JWT user (auth.email()) who last wrote this row. Auto-stamped on every INSERT/UPDATE.

Audit: the AI model credited on the last save when an LLM made/assisted the change (e.g. "gpt-4o"). NULL for plain human writes. Read from the app.modified_by_model session GUC by the audit trigger. The owner (CreatedBy/ModifiedBy) is always the human JWT user, never a model.

Lifecycle status (mirrors ERBFeatureStatuses keys). DESIGNED for not-yet-built.

A subject state instance's name is the same as its subject state instance ID.

In plain words

Subject state instance ID.

FK -> StateMachines.StateMachineId.

A pointer to State Machine. It is not derived from anything else — it is the link the rest of the DAG hangs off.

Polymorphic PK of the subject row.

The machine state entered by this occupancy record.

Timestamp when the subject left this state. NULL while current.

1-based position on this subject's path through the machine.

Consumers 1 direct rules that read this one

Self-FK -> SubjectStateInstances.SubjectStateInstanceId — the previous occupancy in this subject's chain. NULL for the initial state.

A pointer to Subject State Instance. It is not derived from anything else — it is the link the rest of the DAG hangs off.

FK -> StateTransitions.StateTransitionId — the edge event that created this occupancy.

A pointer to State Transition. It is not derived from anything else — it is the link the rest of the DAG hangs off.

The violation type's is school eligible by cap is determined by the following priority:

  1. true if the points is at most the traffic school point cap
  2. false in all other cases
In plain words

True when points is at most traffic school point cap.

As a formula
= IF(Points <= Traffic School Point Cap, TRUE, FALSE)

License-points state machine for the driver: Suspended at/above the suspension threshold, Warning at/above the warning threshold, otherwise Valid.

In Docs

The driver's license status is determined by the following priority:

  1. “Suspended” if the active points is at least the suspension threshold
  2. “Warning” if the active points is at least the warning threshold
  3. “Valid” in all other cases
In plain words

If active points is at least suspension threshold then "Suspended", otherwise if active points is at least warning threshold then "Warning", otherwise "Valid".

As a formula
= IF(Active Points >= Suspension Threshold, "Suspended", IF(Active Points >= Warning Threshold, "Warning", "Valid"))

ƒ Contest Status Calculated 3 hops from ground truth string DR-177

Contest/Hearing state machine: NotContested when the driver did not elect to contest; otherwise HearingRequested -> Scheduled -> Heard, reflected from the latest hearing's outcome.

In Docs

The citation's contest status is determined by the following priority:

  1. “NotContested” if the contest requested flag is not set
  2. “HearingRequested” if the count of hearings is 0
  3. “Scheduled” if any of these hold:
    • the latest hearing outcome is “Pending”
    • the latest hearing outcome is blank
  4. “Heard” in all other cases
In plain words

If not contest requested then "NotContested", otherwise if count of hearings equals 0 then "HearingRequested", otherwise if latest hearing outcome is "Pending" or latest hearing outcome is blank then "Scheduled", otherwise "Heard".

As a formula
= IF(NOT(Contest Requested), "NotContested", IF(Count of Hearings = 0, "HearingRequested", IF(OR(Latest Hearing Outcome = "Pending", ISBLANK(Latest Hearing Outcome)), "Scheduled", "Heard")))
Inputs 3 fields this rule reads
●Contest RequestedCitation Whether the driver elected to contest the citation (request a hearing) rather than pay. ΣCount of HearingsCitation Count of hearings whose citation is this one. ƒ Is Guilty Calculated 4 hops from ground truth boolean DR-179

True when the driver is liable: either found guilty/upheld at hearing, or defaulted by missing the response deadline without contesting.

In Docs

The citation's is guilty is determined by the following priority:

  1. true if any of these hold:
    • the latest hearing outcome is “Guilty”
    • the latest hearing outcome is “Upheld”
    • all of these hold:
      • the response overdue flag is set
      • the contest requested flag is not set
  2. false in all other cases
In plain words

True when latest hearing outcome is "Guilty", latest hearing outcome is "Upheld", or is response overdue and not contest requested.

As a formula
= IF(OR(Latest Hearing Outcome = "Guilty", Latest Hearing Outcome = "Upheld", AND(Is Response Overdue, NOT(Contest Requested))), TRUE, FALSE)
Inputs 3 fields this rule reads

Amount currently owed: 0 if dismissed; otherwise the base fine plus the jurisdiction's late penalty if the payment is late.

In Docs

The citation's amount due USD is determined by the following priority:

  1. 0 if the dismissed flag is set
  2. the base fine USD times 1 plus the late penalty pct if the payment late flag is set
  3. the base fine USD in all other cases
In plain words

If is dismissed then 0, otherwise if is payment late then (base fine USD times (1 plus late penalty pct)), otherwise base fine USD.

As a formula
= IF(Is Dismissed, 0, IF(Is Payment Late, Base Fine USD * (1 + Late Penalty Pct), Base Fine USD))

ƒ Payment Status Calculated 7 hops from ground truth string DR-185

Payment/Penalty state machine: NotOwed (dismissed) -> Paid -> Collections -> Late -> Due. Evaluated in priority order.

In Docs

The citation's payment status is determined by the following priority:

  1. “NotOwed” if the dismissed flag is set
  2. “Paid” if the paid on has a value
  3. “Collections” if the in collections flag is set
  4. “Late” if the payment late flag is set
  5. “Due” if the guilty flag is set
  6. “Pending” in all other cases
In plain words

If is dismissed then "NotOwed", otherwise if not paid on is blank then "Paid", otherwise if is in collections then "Collections", otherwise if is payment late then "Late", otherwise if is guilty then "Due", otherwise "Pending".

As a formula
= IF(Is Dismissed, "NotOwed", IF(NOT(ISBLANK(Paid on)), "Paid", IF(Is in Collections, "Collections", IF(Is Payment Late, "Late", IF(Is Guilty, "Due", "Pending")))))
Inputs 5 fields this rule reads
ƒIs DismissedCitation True when latest hearing outcome is "Dismissed". ●Paid onCitation Date the fine was paid in full. Null if not yet paid. ƒIs in CollectionsCitation True when is payment late and as of date is greater than collections deadline. ƒIs Payment LateCitation True when is guilty, paid on is blank, and as of date is greater than payment due date. ƒIs GuiltyCitation True when latest hearing outcome is "Guilty", latest hearing outcome is "Upheld", or is response overdue and not contest requested.

ƒ Citation Status Calculated 4 hops from ground truth string DR-187

Citation lifecycle state machine: Issued -> Responded -> InContest -> Adjudicated -> Closed. The top-level status synthesizing the other tracks.

In Docs

The citation's citation status is determined by the following priority:

  1. “Closed” if any of these hold:
    • the paid on has a value
    • the dismissed flag is set
  2. “Adjudicated” if any of these hold:
    • the latest hearing outcome is “Guilty”
    • the latest hearing outcome is “Upheld”
    • all of these hold:
      • the response overdue flag is set
      • the contest requested flag is not set
  3. “InContest” if all of these hold:
    • the contest requested flag is set
    • the count of hearings is greater than 0
  4. “Responded” if the responded on has a value
  5. “Issued” in all other cases
In plain words

If not paid on is blank or is dismissed then "Closed", otherwise if latest hearing outcome is "Guilty", latest hearing outcome is "Upheld", or is response overdue and not contest requested then "Adjudicated", otherwise if contest requested and count of hearings is greater than 0 then "InContest", otherwise if not responded on is blank then "Responded", otherwise "Issued".

As a formula
= IF(OR(NOT(ISBLANK(Paid on)), Is Dismissed), "Closed", IF(OR(Latest Hearing Outcome = "Guilty", Latest Hearing Outcome = "Upheld", AND(Is Response Overdue, NOT(Contest Requested))), "Adjudicated", IF(AND(Contest Requested, Count of Hearings > 0), "InContest", IF(NOT(ISBLANK(Responded on)), "Responded", "Issued"))))
Inputs 7 fields this rule reads
●Paid onCitation Date the fine was paid in full. Null if not yet paid. ƒIs DismissedCitation True when latest hearing outcome is "Dismissed". ΣLatest Hearing OutcomeCitation Largest outcome across all hearings whose citation is this one and scheduled for is largest scheduled for across all hearings whose citation is this one. ƒIs Response OverdueCitation True when responded on is blank and as of date is greater than response due date. ●Contest RequestedCitation Whether the driver elected to contest the citation (request a hearing) rather than pay. ΣCount of HearingsCitation Count of hearings whose citation is this one. ●Responded onCitation Date the driver responded (paid or requested a hearing). Null if no response yet.

Case Event

A case event is identified by its name and is related to a citation.

ƒ Name Calculated 1 hop from ground truth string DR-192

Kebab-cased PK derived from the event reference number.

In Docs ⚠︎ mechanical

A case event's name is computed as the lower-cased event number with every a space replaced by a hyphen.

In plain words

Event number lowercased with “ ” replaced by “-”.

As a formula
= SUBSTITUTE(LOWER(Event Number), " ", "-")
Inputs 1 fields this rule reads
●Event NumberCase Event Human event reference number (sortable, e.g. 'EV-2026-0001').

Human event reference number (sortable, e.g. 'EV-2026-0001').

Consumers 1 direct rules that read this one
↗ Citation Label Case Event
↗ Citation Label Lookup 1 hop from ground truth string DR-193

Citation number this event concerns.

In Docs

A case event's citation label is the citation number of the case event's citation.

In plain words

The citation number of the linked citation.

= INDEX(Citation Number, MATCH(Citation, Citation ID, 0))
Inputs 3 fields this rule reads

Ground truth at the leaves 3 the raw values this ultimately depends on
● Citation Number Citation ⇢ Citation Case Event ● Citation ID Citation
● Occurred on Ground truth date

Date the event occurred.

● Track Ground truth string

Which state machine this transition belongs to: 'Citation', 'Contest', 'Payment', or 'License'.

● From State Ground truth string

Prior state on the track (null for the initial event).

● To State Ground truth string

New state on the track after this transition.

● Note Ground truth string

Free-text note describing the transition.

● Created At Ground truth datetime

Audit: when this row was first inserted. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on INSERT); immutable thereafter.

● Created by Ground truth string

Audit: the OWNER — the JWT user (auth.email()) who created this row. Auto-stamped on INSERT; immutable thereafter. NULL for build-time seed rows (no signed-in user).

● Modified At Ground truth datetime

Audit: when this row was last written. Auto-stamped by the audit trigger (now() on every INSERT/UPDATE).

● Modified by Ground truth string

Audit: the JWT user (auth.email()) who last wrote this row. Auto-stamped on every INSERT/UPDATE.

● Modified by Model Ground truth string

Audit: the AI model credited on the last save when an LLM made/assisted the change (e.g. "gpt-4o"). NULL for plain human writes. Read from the app.modified_by_model session GUC by the audit trigger. The owner (CreatedBy/ModifiedBy) is always the human JWT user, never a model.
